penalties: Non-compliance with placement policy results in suspension or disciplinary action as specified in Section 6.
Withdrawal from a company after selection without valid approval is treated as a violation and may be reported to the Student Disciplinary Committee (STDC).
Misrepresentation of information in CV, portfolio, or documents results in disciplinary action by the Student Disciplinary Committee (STDC).
Tampering with documents, offer letters, or providing false documentation results in immediate disciplinary action.
Failure to join an organization after selection without reason may be referred to the Student Disciplinary Committee (STDC).
Direct communication with recruiters without express permission from CAR is treated as a violation.
Missing a maximum of three (3) placement drives consecutively without prior written approval results in being declared out of the placement process for the ongoing cycle.
Non-participation, withdrawal, or refusal without approval is treated in accordance with the disciplinary mechanism outlined in Section 6.

clauses.heading: Section 5
clauses.text: The Career & Alumni Relations (CAR) is the central body responsible for planning, coordinating, and executing all placement and career-readiness activities across all Schools of RV University. It functions as the primary institutional interface for recruiters and ensures transparency and operational consistency in all placement-related processes. The responsibilities include, but are not limited to: a. Coordinating placement and internship activities across all Schools of the University. b. Designing and delivering pre-placement training in collaboration with Schools and external partners. c. Facilitating recruiter engagement, recruitment processes, and managing campus drives end-to-end. d. Ensuring strict compliance with the Placement Policy across all Schools. e. Acting as the institutional contact for student and recruiter queries related to placement processes, and forwarding any grievances to the appropriate University authorities. f. Maintaining open communication with School leadership to ensure seamless coordination for all placement-related activities.
clauses.plain_english: This clause defines the Career & Alumni Relations (CAR) department as the central authority for managing all placement and internship activities at RV University, including training, recruiter coordination, and policy enforcement.
clauses.risk_justification: This is a standard administrative definition of departmental roles and responsibilities within a university setting.
obligations: Plan, coordinate, and execute placement and career-readiness activities
Facilitate recruiter engagement and manage campus drives
Ensure compliance with the Placement Policy
Act as institutional contact for placement queries

summary.executive_summary: This Placement Policy outlines the governance, operational structure, and eligibility criteria for placement and internship activities facilitated by the Career & Alumni Relations (CAR) department at RV University. It establishes mandatory conduct standards for students, including attendance requirements, offer acceptance protocols, and documentation submission. The policy grants the University broad discretionary powers to modify rules, withhold placement opportunities, and impose disciplinary actions for non-compliance. It serves as the primary regulatory framework for all students participating in recruitment processes from the 2022 graduating batch onwards.
key_points: The Career & Alumni Relations (CAR) department is the sole authority for coordinating all placement and internship activities.
Students must maintain 80% attendance in pre-placement training and have no backlogs to remain eligible.
The '1x Offer' rule dictates that a student is considered placed upon securing one confirmed offer, regardless of acceptance.
Students are required to report all off-campus offers to the School Chairperson or Placement Officer for record-keeping.
The University reserves the right to unilaterally modify placement rules, eligibility criteria, and withhold placement services for violations.
Non-compliance with the policy may result in suspension or other disciplinary actions.
red_flags: The policy lacks a formal dispute resolution mechanism, leaving students without a clear path to challenge administrative decisions.
The University maintains broad, unilateral rights to modify the policy and withhold services without defined procedural safeguards for students.
The '1x Offer' rule and 'Offer Progression' rules create significant pressure on students to accept the first offer received, potentially limiting career choices.
The policy is missing essential clauses such as Force Majeure, Governing Law, and specific Data Protection provisions required under Indian law.
favorable_clauses: Section 27 provides a mechanism for interpretation and clarification of policy ambiguities through the Director of CAR and the Registrar's Office.
Section 16 defines 'Dream Offers' to allow students to pursue higher-value opportunities, providing a structured path for career advancement beyond initial placements.
unusual_clauses: Section 10 (Basic Offer Rule) considers a student 'placed' the moment their name appears in a selection list, regardless of whether the student has accepted the offer or the offer letter has been issued.
Section 28 grants the University the right to impose additional conditions based on academic performance or recruiter feedback at its sole discretion.
recommended_actions: Request the inclusion of a formal grievance redressal or dispute resolution process to protect student interests.
Seek clarification on the '1x Offer' rule to ensure students have a reasonable window to evaluate offers before being marked as 'placed'.
Advise the University to incorporate a Data Privacy clause to ensure compliance with the India DPDP Act 2023 regarding the handling of student personal data.
Recommend the addition of a 'Force Majeure' clause to address potential disruptions to the placement process beyond the control of either party.
Ensure that the policy is reviewed by legal counsel to align with Indian employment and educational regulations, particularly regarding disciplinary procedures.
